subject: Immediate: Nimbus Labs dedicated GPU headroom exhausted – urgent remediation
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah@nimbuslabs.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sre@nimbuslabs.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden latency/error spike on dedicated pool (Nimbus)

David —

We started seeing a ramp in 95th/99th latency and elevated 5xx rates on our reserved capacity (dedicated pool) around 14:45 PDT. Token throughput dropped ~40% on the pinned pool and requests began queueing. This is directly impacting several user-facing flows.

Quick facts:
- Affected environment: nimbus-prod (reserved pool: nimbus-dedicated-vertical-2)
- Symptoms: 5–8x increase in tail latency, 3% -> 12% 5xx rate on generation endpoints, completed tokens per second down ~40%
- First observed: 2027-06-13T14:45:22Z
- We've attached a small support bundle and a Grafana screenshot showing queue depth + GPU utilization.

We need an immediate ETA on mitigation. This is blocking our payments path and our renewal conversation is active; we need to understand: is this a capacity saturation issue or an internal scheduling regression?

Please escalate.

—Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of SRE, Nimbus Labs
Attachments: support_bundle.zip (log tar), nimbus_grafana.png
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 15:46:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency/error spike on dedicated pool (Nimbus)

Looping infra + eng leadership.

Summary: Nimbus (reserved) reports sustained tail latency spike and throughput collapse in their dedicated GPU pool; they attached logs and Grafana. They claim token throughput down ~40% and 5xxs rising. Initial theory: either noisy tenant encroachment (non-dedicated workloads landing on the nodes) or a scheduler/autoscaler regression that reduced effective headroom.

Immediate asks:
- Grace: can you validate whether any recent scheduler or kernel rollout touched the nimbus-dedicated-vertical-2 node group in the 13:30–15:00 PDT window? Check preemption logs and kube-scheduler traces.
- Vivek / Rishi: I need executive approval for an emergency 20% burst (chargeable to Redwood for now) and an SLA credit discussion if this is our fault — cc'ing Marissa to keep the account team in the loop for communication.

I'll schedule a short bridge (30 min) in 10 minutes; please join if you can.

Attachments referenced by customer: nimbus_grafana.png, support_bundle.zip

—David
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 16:02:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency/error spike on dedicated pool (Nimbus)

David / team —

Initial findings (quick triage):
- We saw a scheduling instability on the dedicated node group at ~14:39 PDT: several pods in nimbus-dedicated-vertical-2 were rescheduled simultaneously. Kernel-ABI pinned change was rolled to the fleet at 13:50 PDT (small change to memory allocator behavior).
- There are also signs of a small batch of stage/dev workloads that did not respect the node-labels and were scheduled onto one of the dedicated nodes between 14:05–14:20 PDT (scheduling log attached: scheduling_log.txt). That increased local contention and pushed the autoscaler to make reactive decisions that reduced the apparent headroom for the pinned tenancy.

Short-term mitigations we will apply now:
1) Cordon the two affected dedicated nodes and drain non-nimbus pods (fast).
2) Revert the kernel-ABI allocator change on the dedicated pool (rollback in progress).
3) Temporarily open a controlled burst from shared pool to cover 25% of Nimbus traffic for next 4 hours (requires exec sign-off for billing/credit).

Impact if we do nothing: sustained errors and potential SLA breach; customer renewal could be at risk.

I'll post post-mortem artifacts to the incident link and update the bridge.

—Grace
Head of Infra Reliability
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 16:12:47 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden latency/error spike on dedicated pool (Nimbus)

Vivek / Rishi —

Per Grace's triage the likely root cause is (a) a small scheduler mis-label that allowed non-dedicated workloads onto a dedicated node and (b) a coincident allocator kernel change that amplified tail latencies. Grace proposes: revert kernel change + cordon/drain the affected nodes + open a temporary burst from shared capacity to stop user-visible errors.

Approve two things so we can move fast:
1) Emergency burst capacity for Nimbus: approve Redwood to serve up to 25% of Nimbus production volume from our shared fleet for the next 4 hours. We'll track token usage separately and absorb the cost for the immediate window; we can negotiate credits with Nimbus if we confirm platform fault.
2) Approval to offer Nimbus a one-time credit of up to 30% of this month's committed invoice if post-mortem blames our scheduling/kernel changes. This is an exec-level concession and would be communicated by the account team.

This is time-sensitive — Grace is about to drain nodes and start the rollback. I recommend a quick thumbs-up so the burst goes live and customer errors stop.

—David
From: Sarah Lee <sarah@nimbuslabs.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@nimbuslabs.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency/error spike on dedicated pool (Nimbus)

Thanks for the quick triage and the bridge earlier. The controlled burst started around 16:05 PDT and we saw immediate improvement in tail latency and error rate — thank you.

Two asks from Nimbus:
1) Please confirm the root cause and the corrective actions in writing, including the rollback details and the scheduling fix.
2) We expect this incident to be reflected in the SLA review and to receive a proposed credit within 48 hours — our renewal committee will want formal language.

Please let us know the timeline for the post-mortem and credit proposal.

—Sarah
Head of SRE, Nimbus Labs
